findings.asked: Equation of a normal to a curve containing a negative power.
findings.wentWrong: Some could not differentiate -3x to the minus 1 even after doing so earlier; some wrote the curve as y = -3x to the minus 1 + c and read the gradient as -3; credit was given for knowing the normal's gradient is the negative reciprocal.
findings.rule: The gradient of a curve comes from dy/dx at the point, never from a coefficient.

findings.asked: A gradient condition on a tangent.
findings.wentWrong: Few managed the first step of writing the tangent's gradient as the given value (-8), so nothing followed.
findings.rule: A stated tangent gradient is an equation: dy/dx = that value.

findings.asked: Equation of a normal at a given x.
findings.wentWrong: Well done with advance notice; losses were arithmetic in the gradient at x = -1 or in the constant.
findings.rule: Evaluate dy/dx carefully at the point, then negative reciprocal, then substitute.

findings.asked: Tangent and normal to a curve given a line's gradient.
findings.wentWrong: Many set the line equal to the curve instead of differentiating; others used the given gradient 3 wrongly and so had the wrong normal gradient.
findings.rule: Parallel to a line means dy/dx equals that line's gradient; perpendicular means the negative reciprocal.

findings.asked: Differentiate, then substitute y into a relation involving dy/dx.
findings.wentWrong: Differentiation was fine (x to the minus 2 written for x to the minus 4, +12 for -12). Part (ii) was poorly answered: candidates solved dy/dx = 0 instead of substituting the expression for y into the given relation.
findings.rule: Read the condition: it may link y and dy/dx rather than set dy/dx to zero.

findings.asked: Point where the gradient is 5, then the coordinates of a point on the normal.
findings.wentWrong: Many solved 6x - 5 = 0 instead of 6x - 5 = 5; in (ii) the perpendicular gradient -1/5 was found but candidates stopped there, reused part (i) values, or gave a line equation when coordinates were asked.
findings.rule: dy/dx = the stated gradient; then answer in the form requested.

ruleToRemember: Tangent gradient = dy/dx at the point; normal gradient = -1 / (dy/dx); 'the gradient is 5' means dy/dx = 5, not 0; check whether an equation or coordinates are wanted.
aStarSignal: A derivative condition that is not zero (a given gradient, or a relation between y and dy/dx) recognised and used correctly.
